sections.overview: This Chiapas catfish is the only described species in its own family, Lacantuniidae, and its placement among catfish lineages remains unresolved.
sections.identification: It can exceed 42 cm standard length and has several unique skull, gill-arch and gas-bladder structures.
sections.habitat: It occupies deep channels and pools in the Lacantún and Lacanjá rivers, with rocks and strong eddy currents.
sections.diet: Gut contents include fish, crabs, prawns and large, tough seeds.
sections.behavior: It has been collected at night in fast-flowing reaches and is commonly caught by local fishers.
sections.reproduction: Its reproductive biology remains poorly known; a Chiapas survey collected adults but no juveniles.
sections.ecology: Its unusual anatomy has resisted confident placement among other catfish families, so close relatives have not been identified.
sections.conservation: CONABIO reports a Vulnerable global assessment and lists it as endangered under Mexican law.
